executive_summary: Tech Mahindra’s September result shows the turnaround progressing from cost repair toward a broader growth recovery. Constant-currency growth and recurring large-deal wins improve the evidence, but the investment case at the current premium requires cash conversion and continued margin execution; local PAT and EPS definitions need reconciliation before an exact target.
research_stance: Constructive turnaround evidence, with valuation and data-basis reconciliation limiting precision.

thesis_drivers.title: Recovery is broader than INR translation
thesis_drivers.evidence: The call reports 7.2% YoY constant-currency growth, including 7.0% organic CC growth, versus 15.6% INR growth. Communications and other verticals expanded; foreign exchange and a small inorganic contribution must be separated from organic demand.
thesis_drivers.source: September 2026 local financials and latest earnings-call transcript

thesis_drivers.title: Margin repair approaches its quantified milestone
thesis_drivers.evidence: Management reported EBIT margin 14.8%, up 40 bp QoQ and 260 bp YoY, and retained 15% FY27 target. Local operating profit is closer to EBITDA; using its approximately 18% OPM as EBIT would materially misread the turnaround.
thesis_drivers.source: September 2026 local financials and latest earnings-call transcript

thesis_drivers.title: Growth must show up in cash
thesis_drivers.evidence: Call-reported DSO 88 days rose 4 days QoQ; rebadged deal ramp-up affected quarterly cash flow. The 90–100% annual FCF/PAT goal provides a test of earnings quality and deal execution.
thesis_drivers.source: September 2026 local financials and latest earnings-call transcript

Revenue ₹16,180.0 crore was +15.6% YoY and+3.0% QoQ. The call reports 7.2% YoY constant-currency growth, including 7.0% organic CC growth, versus 15.6% INR growth. Communications and other verticals expanded; foreign exchange and a small inorganic contribution must be separated from organic demand.

business_economics: The turnaround depends on winning and expanding multi-year engagements while preserving the cash return on delivery. Total CC growth of 7.2% includes organicCC7.0%; reported-dollar 6.8% and INR15.6% are different currency lenses. Management’s large-client evidence is useful: >$20 m accounts grew 11.7% YoY and 3.1% QoQ, rather than a supposed 11.7% attrition statistic.

The $1.023 billion new-deal TCV and $4.270 billion LTM wins support pipeline conversion, but contract value is not revenue and has no universal annual conversion factor. Rebadging and transition costs can front-load people and working capital before steady-state collections.
earnings_quality: The local operating-profit figure is reconciled:₹2,878 crore less depreciation ₹491 crore equals the call’s ₹2,387 crore EBIT. This makes the local 18% OPM versus 14.8% EBIT margin a definition difference, not an earnings discrepancy.

The tax rate was 29.9% versus 26.6% excluding a one-time item, while reported PAT ₹1,586 crore still differs from local ₹1,610 crore. Normalize tax only on a consistent reporting perimeter; it does not independently explain the ₹24 crore gap or establish an adjusted EPS.
capital_allocation: Quarterly FCF of $135 million relative to $166 million PAT is about 81%, below management’s 90–100% full-year ambition. That does not make the annual commitment missed, but it makes the expected next-quarter normalization of rebadged-deal cash conversion a concrete test. DSO 88 days rose 4 days sequentially.

The policy of returning 85%+of FCF depends on collecting cash, not just meeting EBIT margin targets. A proposed 1:1 bonus issue changes units; it is not an additional economic distribution. Customer concentration, delivery commitments and AI-related investment must be measured against cash returns on new engagements.
valuation_logic: The dated 30.4 x P/E should be judged against sustainable attributable earnings and cash conversion, not a perpetual continuation of margin repair. The stated 15% FY27 EBIT-margin target is near current 14.8%, so a substantial further rerating needs demand growth and cash conversion as well as completion of the cost program.

No price target is given until PAT attribution, diluted share count and proposed bonus basis are reconciled. The earlier alternate EPS ₹17.84 claim lacked a traceable primary source in the reviewed set and has been withdrawn. This is an evidence correction, not an explanation of why a different published number might exist elsewhere.
peer_positioning: TCS, Infosys and HCL Technologies are useful delivery-scale comparisons, but telecom exposure, margin maturity, deal mix and capital returns differ. TechM should not automatically receive a mature peer’s multiple before sustaining organic growth and cash conversion through large-deal ramps. AI partnership announcements are weaker evidence than disclosed recurring revenue and customer-level economics.
